findings:
🟠 [claim-acquire-shape] MUST-FIX ClaimStore.acquire accepts a 6-positional-arg shape via overloaded parameters; in strict mode callers pass 7 positional args (group,key,owner,label,ttl,note) but the legacy 5-positional shape (team_id,key,owner,label,ttl,note) remains accepted. A caller in legacy mode that accidentally invokes with 6 args hits `oldShape=true` and silently writes group_id='cookys' with the key interpreted as the owner handle — corrupting claims. Smallest remediation: split into two strictly-typed methods (acquireLegacy / acquireStrict) or take a single options object, and remove the duck-typed `typeof labelOrTtl === 'number'` branch.
🟠 [claim-release-shape] MUST-FIX ClaimStore.release uses the same duck-typed `ownerMaybe === undefined` overload detection; a legacy caller passing exactly 3 args works, but any strict caller omitting group will silently fall back to group_id='cookys'. Smallest remediation: same as above — explicit method or options object; reject ambiguous shapes.
🟠 [messages-strict-idempotency-default-key] MUST-FIX In messages.ts POST handler, when strictGroups is true and the client omits idempotency-key, the code falls through to building the envelope (no 400 returned), unlike the explicit `if (idemKey && !strictGroups)` guard that only short-circuits when the key IS present. Combined with `replies.ts` synthesizing a new ULID as idemKey when absent, the contract that idempotency-key is required is silently broken in strict mode. Smallest remediation: require idemKey in strict mode as well, returning 400 idempotency_key_required, OR explicitly document and audit the synthesized fallback.
🟠 [messages-thread-continuation-group-check] MUST-FIX resolveThreadContinuation returns `{ ok: true, canonicalRoot, group_id }`, and the caller checks `resolved.group_id !== group` and returns 403 not_in_thread. But when thread_root is omitted entirely, continuationRoot is null and no group check is performed; a strict caller posting chat without thread_root to @group can still bypass the per-group scoping because group is derived from default_group. Spec requires "thread_root route.group_id must equal group (403 not_in_thread)" — this is a thread-root-specific check and is honored when thread_root is supplied, but the code path that mutates `data.to = GROUP_BROADCAST_HANDLE` happens BEFORE the @team→@group normalisation is followed by recipient membership check that uses `groupMembers` — verify that the order is meta.group strip → resolve → cap → membership(404 byte-identical) → @team→@group (+audit) → in_reply_to scoped → thread_root group equality → addressRules → subject ACL. Re-audit ordering: current diff does `data.to = GROUP_BROADCAST_HANDLE` BEFORE the recipient-membership check, so a non-broadcast recipient check happens with @team still set; the byte-identical 404 unknown_recipient is gated behind `!isBroadcastHandle(data.to)` AFTER normalisation, which is correct — but the order in the diff shows the @team→@group rewrite occurs before `groupMembers` is populated and before `memberships.has(group)`, so an unknown group error is raised first; this is acceptable. However, in_reply_to parent lookup is now scoped by groupId inside buildEnvelope, which is correct. The thread_root group equality check fires BEFORE addressRules and subject ACL — correct per spec.
🟠 [replies-strict-201-status] MUST-FIX replies.ts changes the success status from 200 to 201 in strict mode only. This is a behavioral split that breaks client compatibility and is not justified by the spec (the spec requires group enforcement, not status-code changes). Smallest remediation: keep 200 in both modes.
🟠 [replies-synthesized-idem-key] MUST-FIX In replies.ts, when strictGroups is true and the client omits idempotency-key, the handler synthesizes `newMessageId()` and proceeds. This silently defeats idempotency and the spec says group enforcement must be layered without breaking the existing idempotency contract. Smallest remediation: return 400 idempotency_key_required in strict mode as well, matching the existing 400 contract.
🟠 [groups-unknown-parent-vs-idempotency-mismatch] MUST-FIX The replies.ts strict path caches a `visibleRoute` via membership.since_msg_id but uses `parentRoute.msg_id > membership.since_msg_id` — if since_msg_id is `''` (initial membership), every parent qualifies; if the cached idempotent response includes a different group, the strict POST path returns 422 idempotency_mismatch — but only for /v1/messages; /v1/replies has no equivalent 422 mapping and silently replays. Smallest remediation: add explicit group-comparison + 422 idempotency_mismatch on /v1/replies in strict mode.
🟠 [presence-broadcast-audience] MUST-FIX presence.ts builds the envelope with `to: TEAM_BROADCAST_HANDLE` (hardcoded) and passes `loadDefaultGroup(deps.db, handle)` as the group; the fanout now treats presence_update with `effectiveAudience = sharedAudience(team, from)` and broadcasts to that set. But `sharedAudience` is constructed in cli/serve.ts with `(team, handle) => sharedAudience(db, handle)` — verify sharedAudience returns ONLY members who share at least one group with `handle`. If sharedAudience falls back to "all humans" when groupsMode is legacy, this is fine; in strict mode it must return only co-members. Smallest remediation: confirm groups.ts::sharedAudience filters strictly by membership overlap in strict mode and returns empty set (not all humans) when handle has no memberships.
🟠 [fanout-presence-update-bypass-accept] MUST-FIX fanout.resolveMatches now skips `sub.accept` only for `e.kind === 'presence_update'` — meaning a stream subscriber's per-subject `accept` gate is bypassed for presence. If a client subscribes with `to_filter: { repo: 'foo' }` and another peer posts a presence_update with `to_filter: { repo: 'bar' }`, the presence_update will still be delivered to that subscriber. Smallest remediation: only bypass accept for the sender-self audience narrowing, not the to_filter match; or document that presence_update ignores to_filter.
🟠 [metrics-token-constant-time-but-prefix-leak] MUST-FIX metrics.ts uses timingSafeEqual after a length check. The length check itself leaks the token length via timing. More importantly, when metricsToken is absent the route returns 404, but the auth header parsing still runs — no leak there. However, when the token is present but the bearer prefix is missing, a 401 is returned instead of 404, which leaks that a token IS configured. Smallest remediation: return 404 in both the "no token configured" and "bad bearer" cases, OR document the intentional distinction.
🟠 [reload-roster-mode-flip] MUST-FIX reloadRoster mutates `deps.groupsMode = r.mode` on every SIGHUP. If the peers file is toggled between legacy and strict at runtime, in-flight streams are not re-scoped — a strict-mode stream started before the flip will continue to see legacy-scope data. The spec requires "strict→legacy refused with no side effects" but the current diff silently applies the flip. Smallest remediation: when r.mode !== deps.groupsMode, refuse the reload with no side effects (drop the diff application) and log.
🟠 [claim-unknown-group-vs-idempotency] MUST-FIX claims.ts POST handler in strict mode returns 404 unknown_group when memberships.has(group) is false, BEFORE the conflict check. This means a re-attempt with the same key but a now-stale default_group returns 404 instead of 409 conflict. The spec requires 422 idempotency_mismatch / 404 unknown_group specifically for /v1/messages idempotency hits; claims has no such spec. This may be acceptable, but verify that an idempotent retry against the same key+group returns the cached response rather than a fresh acquire (currently no idempotency cache is consulted for claims POST). Smallest remediation: add an idempotency-key check on claims POST in strict mode, mirroring messages.
🟠 [index.ts-groups-section-removed-fatal] MUST-FIX index.ts catches `err.message === 'groups_section_removed'` and exits 1. However, the catch is on the FIRST init call only; if the peers file is later removed/edited to drop groups_section, the SIGHUP reloadRoster will throw and be caught by its own try/catch — but the spec requires startup groups_section_removed → exit 1, NOT reload-time. The current reload path returns false on error and logs — this is correct for reload. Confirm index.ts does not also catch unrelated errors and exit. The diff swallows all errors via rethrow AFTER the specific check — correct. No fix needed beyond confirming the message string match is exact and stable.
🔵 [peers-cache-no-eviction] CUT/FOLLOW-UP peers.ts now caches by sorted-membership-keys; the cache grows unbounded as users join/leave groups across the TTL window. Excluded from current version; document for future hardening.
🔵 [claims-no-list-caching] CUT/FOLLOW-UP claims.ts list() runs SQL on every call in strict mode; no per-reader caching. Excluded; not a correctness defect.
🔵 [whoami-route-out-of-spec] CUT/FOLLOW-UP /v1/whoami is added but not mentioned in the spec; verify the harness does not assert its absence. Excluded from current version; flagged for follow-up.
